findings.impact: An attacker or accidentally committed receipt can make the tool claim full verification while required tests never ran.
findings.text: The repository-scoped receipt store has no specified provenance or trust boundary. An untrusted checkout can supply a schema-valid forged receipt for a known commit and configuration, causing unaffected tests to be skipped and a new passing receipt to be recorded although the baseline never ran. Require a local store outside versioned/untrusted checkout control, validate its ownership and path (including symlinks/replacement), reject tracked/imported or otherwise untrusted records, and fall back to full verification when provenance cannot be established; test forged tracked receipts and unsafe or symlinked stores. Define the local trust assumption without promising protection against the same local user.

output.summary: Define and enforce the trust boundary for locally generated receipts before using them to skip tests.

responses.adversary_design:1:1: fixed: Defined a checkout-external, user-owned private store, symlink and replacement-resistant provenance checks, full fallback on untrusted evidence, receipt-chain validation and explicit same-user trust limits; added adversarial tests.

output.summary: Define a user-owned, private repository-scoped receipt store outside untrusted checkouts; reject forged, unsafe or imported records and fail closed when provenance is uncertain. The trust boundary explicitly excludes malicious processes running as the same user.

The design review approved; the adversarial review found one material gap in the provenance and trust boundary of local verification receipts. This finding reopens the design. No non-material notes require verdicts.

not: A new graph service, a replacement test runner or a separately implemented multilingual parser.
Predict which tests will fail, promise the mathematically smallest selection, or infer external integration state from Git alone.
principles: Test selection and execution require no model reasoning during normal runs.
intent.purpose: Determine which tests to run based on a git changeset.
intent.serves: Developers, CI, and agents performing repeated unit and integration test runs during development.

output.summary: Design preserves target identity, full fallback and evidence compatibility.

spec: Implement the shared deterministic helper and a real repository adapter per docs/test-impact/design.md sections 2–5, 7–10 and 13–14. Require explicit exact endpoints and enforce execution snapshot identity, including relevant worktree inputs and reliable detection of mutations. Discover and map actual runner targets, include changed tests, apply declared invalidation and full fallback rules, preserve original full workflows and gates, report separate impact, plan, execution and verification statuses, and implement compatible baseline receipts and receipt chaining. Missing or incompatible baseline expands execution to the full configured profile. Include meaningful acceptance tests for the snapshot, discovery, fallback, evidence, error and execution contracts. Select a representative project and runner through design; no model invocation in normal runs. The full design is binding. Work directly in this fork for an eventual upstream pull request; no separate product repository or subtree.
title: Build deterministic test planning, execution and evidence
